1What You Will Learn

  • Identify the AWS services and features that secure AI: IAM, KMS, Macie, PrivateLink, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch, VPC, AgentCore Identity and Policy, and Guardrails
  • Describe source citation and data origins
  • Describe secure data engineering and security and privacy considerations
  • Describe hallucination detection and grounding

2Identity, encryption, network, data, agents and data origins

Running case

Cedar and Salt Hardens Its Assistant

  • The security team reviews the booking assistant before launch
  • Questions: who can call the model, where does the data travel, and who can see guest data?
  • The agent will call a booking system for guests
  • They also ask how to prove where an answer came from
  • Your job: choose the controls

Shared Responsibility and Data Protection

  • Under the shared responsibility model, AWS protects the infrastructure; you control your content, access and configuration
  • Amazon Bedrock model providers have no access to its logs, or to your prompts and completions
  • Use multi-factor authentication (MFA) and IAM Identity Center or AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM), so each person gets only the permissions needed
  • Use Transport Layer Security (TLS) (version 1.2 required, 1.3 recommended) and AWS encryption
  • Log activity with AWS CloudTrail
  • Never put sensitive data in tags or free-form name fields

Exam tip: AWS secures the platform; you secure who can use it and what data goes in.

IAM: Roles, Policies and Permissions

Element Use in an AI system
IAM role Gives the application temporary credentials to call a model
IAM policy Allows only needed actions, such as invoking one model
Least privilege Start with no access and add only what is required
Permissions boundaries and conditions Limit what roles can do, and when
Separate roles Different roles to call models, manage guardrails and read training data

Exam tip: Least privilege: roles with narrow policies, never shared long-term keys.

Encryption: AWS KMS and TLS

  • In transit: TLS protects traffic to AWS services
  • At rest: data is encrypted with AWS KMS keys
  • AWS KMS creates and controls keys; keys are held in hardware security modules and never leave KMS unencrypted
  • Use customer managed keys for control, with key policies that limit who can use them
  • Keys can protect Amazon S3 data, guardrails, logs and knowledge base data stores
  • Key use appears in CloudTrail

Exam tip: Encryption at rest with your own control of the key: AWS KMS customer managed keys.

Private Networks: Amazon VPC and AWS PrivateLink

  • AWS PrivateLink makes a private connection between your Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) and Amazon Bedrock
  • You reach Bedrock without an internet gateway, NAT device, VPN or Direct Connect; instances need no public IP
  • You create an interface endpoint, with endpoints for the model runtime, agents and control plane
  • An endpoint policy limits who can do what through the endpoint
  • Use VPC security groups to control traffic to your own resources

Exam tip: Keep model traffic off the internet: a PrivateLink interface endpoint in your VPC.

Amazon Macie: Find Sensitive Data

  • Amazon Macie discovers sensitive data in Amazon S3 by using machine learning and pattern matching
  • It finds PII, financial information and credentials, and you can add custom identifiers
  • It also checks bucket security, such as public access, and creates findings
  • Use it on training data, RAG documents and logs stored in S3
  • Findings flow to EventBridge and AWS Security Hub

Exam tip: Find personal data hiding in S3 files: Amazon Macie.

Secrets Manager and CloudWatch

Service What it does for AI security
AWS Secrets Manager Stores, retrieves and rotates credentials and API keys, so none are hard-coded
Amazon CloudWatch Metrics, logs and alarms; receives Bedrock model invocation logs
Model invocation logging Records prompts, responses and metadata; off by default; to S3 or CloudWatch Logs
AWS CloudTrail Who called which API, for audits

Exam tip: No credentials in code: Secrets Manager. Audit trail of prompts: invocation logging.

Securing Agents: AgentCore Identity and Policy

Feature What it does
AgentCore Identity Identity and credential management for agents; agents act on a user's behalf with secure access and audit trails
Policy in AgentCore Rules, written in Cedar or plain English, checked on every tool call at the Gateway
  • Policy runs outside the agent's code, so a manipulated agent cannot bypass it
  • Decisions are logged in CloudWatch for audits

Exam tip: Who the agent is: AgentCore Identity. What it may do: Policy in AgentCore.

Source Citation and Documenting Data Origins

  • Source citation: the answer shows which documents it used, so users can verify it
  • Data lineage: a record of where data came from and how it changed
  • Data cataloging: an inventory of datasets with owners, meaning and sensitivity
  • On AWS: the AWS Glue Data Catalog and Amazon SageMaker Catalog hold catalog and lineage information
  • Knowledge Bases keep source attribution for RAG answers
  • SageMaker Model Cards document a model's data and use

Exam tip: Prove where data or an answer came from: lineage, cataloging and source citation.

3Privacy, grounding and practice

Secure Data Engineering Beyond the guide

Practice What it means
Assess data quality Check accuracy, completeness and freshness before use
Privacy-enhancing technologies Mask, anonymize or tokenize personal data; add statistical noise where suitable
Data access control Least privilege; retrieve only what the user may see
Data integrity Prevent tampering: validation, versioning, encryption and audit logs

Exam tip: Clean, minimal, protected and traceable data makes a safer AI system.

Security and Privacy Considerations

Concern Control
Prompt injection Prompt design, Guardrails prompt attack filter, least privilege
Data leakage Sensitive information filter, Macie, no secrets in prompts
Output filtering and validation Guardrails, schema checks, human review
Threat detection Amazon GuardDuty finds unusual activity
Vulnerability management Amazon Inspector scans for software flaws
Infrastructure protection VPC, PrivateLink, security groups
Encryption KMS at rest, TLS in transit
Audit trail and toxicity Invocation logs, CloudTrail; content filters

Exam tip: Match the concern to the control: leakage to Macie and filters, injection to Guardrails.

Hallucination Detection and Grounding

  • RAG grounding: answers come from retrieved, trusted documents
  • Contextual grounding check: scores grounding and relevance against the source; below your threshold (0 to 0.99) the answer is blocked
  • Automated Reasoning checks: validate answers against logical rules
  • Output validation: check format, facts and citations before showing an answer
  • Confidence scoring: send low-confidence answers to human review

Exam tip: Ungrounded answer: a contextual grounding check with a threshold, backed by RAG.

What the Exam Asks: Securing AI Systems

  • Which service: IAM, KMS, Macie, PrivateLink, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch, VPC, AgentCore Identity or Policy, Guardrails
  • Which concept: shared responsibility, source citation, data lineage or cataloging
  • Which practice: data quality, privacy-enhancing technologies, access control or integrity
  • Which concern: prompt injection, data leakage, output filtering, logging or toxicity
  • Which method: RAG grounding, output validation or confidence scoring

Exam tip: Name the threat first, then the control.

Design Check: Cedar and Salt's Security Review

What the team needs Name and answer
Only the booking app may call the model An IAM role with a least-privilege policy
Model traffic must stay off the internet PrivateLink interface endpoint
Encrypt knowledge base data with our own keys AWS KMS customer managed key
Find guest emails in S3 training files Amazon Macie
Store the partner API key safely AWS Secrets Manager
Limit what the agent can do with the booking tool Policy in AgentCore; AgentCore Identity for the guest
Show where an answer came from Source citation, lineage and cataloging
Keep an audit trail of prompts Invocation logging and CloudTrail
  • Cover the right column, answer each row yourself, then compare

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1Under the shared responsibility model, which task belongs to the customer when using Amazon Bedrock?

  • ASecuring the physical data centers
  • BControlling access and the data sent to models
  • CMaintaining the global network cables
  • DPatching the service's underlying hardware
Show the answer

Answer: B. AWS protects the infrastructure. The customer controls access, with IAM and MFA, and the data and configuration it puts into the service. Data centers, network cables and hardware are AWS's responsibility.

S2Cedar and Salt wants Amazon Bedrock traffic from its VPC to stay on the AWS network, with no internet gateway. Which feature fits?

  • AAn AWS PrivateLink interface VPC endpoint
  • BA public IP address on every instance
  • CA NAT gateway to the public internet
  • DA larger context window for the model
Show the answer

Answer: A. AWS PrivateLink creates a private connection between a VPC and Amazon Bedrock, with no internet gateway, NAT device or public IP needed. The other options use the internet or do not affect networking.

S3Which TWO actions help prevent data leakage from an AI application? (Select TWO.)

  • AMask personal data with Guardrails sensitive information filters
  • BHard-code API keys in prompts for convenience
  • CUse Amazon Macie to find sensitive data in S3 files
  • DTurn off encryption to make responses faster
  • EShare the production data bucket with the public
Show the answer

Answer: A, C. Sensitive information filters mask PII in prompts and responses, and Macie finds sensitive data in Amazon S3. Hard-coded keys, disabled encryption and public buckets increase leakage risk.

S4A team wants to limit which tools an agent may call and with what inputs, with rules enforced outside the agent's code. Which feature fits?

  • AA larger context window for the agent
  • BPrompt caching for the agent's prompts
  • CA higher temperature for the agent
  • DPolicy in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
Show the answer

Answer: D. Policy in AgentCore intercepts every agent tool call at the Gateway and evaluates it against rules, written in Cedar or natural language, outside the agent's code. The other options do not control tool access.

S5Which approach helps detect hallucinations in a RAG application by comparing answers with the retrieved source?

  • AIncrease the temperature of the model for every request
  • BCache the prompts used in the application to save time
  • CApply a contextual grounding check with a threshold
  • DAdd more epochs to a fine-tuning job on the same data
Show the answer

Answer: C. Contextual grounding checks score how well a response is grounded in the source and relevant to the query, and block responses below the threshold. The other options do not compare an answer with its source.

S6Which AWS service stores database credentials and rotates them, so they are not hard-coded in application code?

  • AAWS Key Management Service
  • BAWS Secrets Manager
  • CAmazon Macie
  • DAmazon CloudWatch
Show the answer

Answer: B. AWS Secrets Manager stores, retrieves and rotates credentials, API keys and other secrets. KMS manages encryption keys, Macie finds sensitive data, and CloudWatch monitors metrics and logs.
